newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Security shrouds Shenzhen hotel before HK handover.
newsitem.headline: Security shrouds Shenzhen hotel before HK handover.

text.p: Security officers have moved into a Shenzhen resort villa where Chinese leaders are expected to stay before they cross the border to Hong Kong for the June 30 handover ceremony, a newspaper said on Thursday.
President Jiang Zemin will attend the event marking Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule at midnight that day, and security has topped the globally-televised agenda.

Jiang and his 100-strong entourage are expected to stop over for one or two days late next week in the southern boom city of Shenzhen, next door to Hong Kong, before entering the territory, the South China Morning Post said.
Ministry of State Security officers are working out contingency plans to cope with any possible "troublesome" situations, the newspaper said but did not disclose its source.
Dozens of officers have started a security sweep at the sprawling 138-room Shenzhen Kylin Villa where Jiang and Prime Minister Li Peng are expected to stay, it said.
The lavish western Shenzhen retreat took 15 months to complete and was opened on Tuesday.
The hotel is now restricted to authorised persons only, it said.
